content_md:
In Relentless Revolution Joyce Appleby talks about how adapting to having a job was really hard because people were used to the suffering of feast and famine but not to consistently working long hours.

We live in much easier times, where having a "job" is still hard but the hard parts often have to do with display of liveness without actually being alive. Displaying affordance of feast when cognitively you are in famine. People becoming slop cannons at work is downstream of playing alive while actually being dead.

The actually alive option would look less human but be even more intimate than how we work now. Instead of displays of humanity such as charismatic speeches and acting excited in the slack channel, you will be sharing ideas more intimately with people through AI mediated media. Think of the standup where everyone performs being on top of things, the all-hands where a VP does a bit to seem relatable, the reacji spam on someone's launch post, the "happy to hop on a call!" Those are displays. The other version is your half-formed notes on why the billing migration keeps breaking getting turned into something a teammate can actually query at 2am, or the way you reason through a messy customer escalation being captured so the next person inherits how you think and not just a ticket. Nobody sees you being excited about it. But someone is closer to your actual mind than any slack thread ever got them.

What you get is a livelier version of a being below an API, where now people get paid whenever their API is called even if they are not present or even working at the same firm anymore. May be you should get royalties for the Nebraska man work that you did several years ago that the company still keeps running. The catch is who owns the API. If the company keeps your captured reasoning and you walk out the door, that isn't intimacy, it's extraction with better tooling. Feast and famine come back, just inverted: the firm feasts on everything you ever figured out and you are back to famine the day you leave. So the alive version only works if the thing below the API stays yours in some real sense. Maybe it's royalties, maybe it's something closer to how musicians license a recording. Otherwise we've just found a more efficient way to be dead at work, except now it keeps going after we're gone.
